chat.why: Hard olympiad maths/physics with short exact answers overlaps the maths share of hle, but chat is mostly puzzles, reading, facts and multiple choice.

math_code.why: The English text-only open-ended maths part (674 problems) is competition maths with a final numeric/expression answer checked automatically, close to math/arxivmath; physics, proof (TP) and image subsets fit less.

olympiadbench.licence: apache-2.0 (Hugging Face card); the GitHub repo states MIT
olympiadbench.summary: 8,476 olympiad and Chinese college-entrance maths and physics problems (Feb 2024, ACL 2024), split into 18 subsets by open-ended vs proof, text-only vs image, English vs Chinese; only about 1,440 are English text-only (674 open-ended maths, 236 open-ended physics, 528 proof). The English open-ended maths set (the one usually called OlympiadBench) is good extra competition-maths data for the math part; anchor scores are on that subset (Qwen2.5-Math report Table 3). No late-2025 frontier score found.

chat.why: Olympiad maths with a short final answer matches only the maths share of hle; the rest of chat is other skills.

math_code.why: One text problem to one final answer across 33 maths sub-domains and 10 difficulty levels, like math/arxivmath; graded by a GPT-4o or Omni-Judge LLM judge (rule-based for a subset) rather than strict boxed matching; no code.

3.model: GPT-5 (on Omni-MATH-2-Filtered, 4,181 cleaned problems, GPT-5-mini judge)

omni_math.summary: 4,428 olympiad-level competition problems (Oct 2024) with difficulty 1-9.5, domain tags, a reference solution and a final answer. Strong candidate for extra hard maths items; a 2026 audit found 61 problems need a missing image, 115 are proofs, 54 are estimation and some reference answers are wrong, so use the cleaned Omni-MATH-2 list. No per-model matrix; only ProcessBench (pragsri8/omnimath) has 1,000 single-model solutions with correctness flags. Overlap with the MATH set was not checked.

chat.why: different skill: writing pandas/numpy code, not answering questions

math_code.why: Code fill-in from a short stub with a comment (StackOverflow-style pandas/numpy tasks), executed against asserts: nearly the ds1000 shape and libraries, but only pandas and numpy and mostly one-line answers.

level_guess.why: No score for the four model groups found. Problems are one-line idioms from high-vote StackOverflow posts (median prompt about 60 tokens); even 2021 Codex 12B passes 18.9% (pandas) / 34.4% (numpy) pass@1 and GPT-3 175B 13-16% (CERT paper Table 4), so modern models should solve most. Kept below 1.0 at L4 because some tests use np.float, removed in NumPy 1.24, which fails on a modern stack.

pandas_numpy_eval.summary: PandasEval and NumpyEval: 101 + 101 HumanEval-style tasks (2022, CERT paper) made from high-vote StackOverflow pandas/numpy posts: a short code context with a comment, the model completes the code, hidden asserts run it. Very close in shape to ds1000 but small, old (likely memorized), mostly one-liners and needing an old NumPy for some tests. DS-1000 is also built from StackOverflow posts; shared source posts were not checked.

chat.why: Competition maths with a short exact answer matches only the maths share of hle.

math_code.why: Fresh 2025 competition problems (algebra, geometry, combinatorics, number theory), one prompt to one final answer parsed and checked exactly, very like math; no code.

3.model: GPT-5 (high), 195 of 212 runs correct (4 runs x 53 problems)

smt_2025.summary: 53 Stanford Math Tournament 2025 problems with exact final answers. Only 53 items, but MathArena publishes every run: 10,875 rows for 43 model configs (GPT-5 family, o3, o4-mini, Gemini 2.5/3 Pro, Claude 3.7/Sonnet 4.5, DeepSeek, Qwen3, GLM, Kimi, Grok...) x 4 runs, with full output, correctness, tokens and cost per run. That is ready-made router training data (quality and cost per model per question). Other measured: Gemini 3 Pro 198/212, Claude Sonnet 4.5 (Think) 178/212. Licence is non-commercial.

chat.why: different skill: writing SQL queries, not answering questions

math_code.why: Code generation checked by running it (execution accuracy), but in SQL over a given database schema rather than Python with pandas/numpy libraries.

agentic.why: different skill: no tool calls, one query output

spider.questions_where: https://huggingface.co/datasets/xlangai/spider (train/dev; test set and the 200 databases from https://yale-lily.github.io/spider)
spider.summary: Spider 1.0 (2018): 10,181 English questions over 200 databases, the model writes a SQL query that is executed and compared with the gold result. A related code skill (data querying) with an executed checker, but SQL not Python, old and heavily trained on; the leaderboard is closed since Feb 2024. The Hugging Face rows hold only question, query and db_id: database files and schemas must be fetched from the Spider site.

chat.why: Very easy one-line word problems with a single number answer could resemble easy private chat items, but chat's public sets are puzzles, reading, facts and MC.

math_code.why: Maths with an exact numeric answer like math, but grade-school one- or two-step arithmetic, far below MATH competition and arxivmath research level.

svamp.summary: SVAMP (NAACL 2021): 1,000 elementary maths word problems (700 train / 300 test) with body, question, equation and numeric answer. Easy, old and heavily trained on; useful only as an easy end of the maths mix (where a cheap model is enough), not for the hard math_code items.

chat.why: different skill: writing programs, not answering questions

math_code.why: Contest programming problems solved with Python and checked on many hidden input/output tests (about 202 per test problem), like LiveCodeBench; algorithmic rather than the library-use code of bigcodebench/ds1000.

2.model: GPT-4 (version not stated; Dec 2023 paper), pass@1 averaged over the 5 difficulty bins of 200 test problems each

taco.summary: TACO (Dec 2023): 26,443 contest programming problems (25,443 train, 1,000 test at 5 difficulty levels) from Codeforces, AtCoder, LeetCode, CodeChef and others, with tests and 1.55M verified Python solutions. A big pool of code items with executable checking; about 70% of problems come from APPS/CodeContests (older, likely memorized), a few rely on images (picture_num), and the Hugging Face copy needs its loading script. GPT-4 scored 31.5% (easy) down to 2% (very hard).

chat.why: University STEM questions (maths, physics, EE&CS, finance) with a short exact answer, close to the STEM parts of hle and mmlu_pro but not multiple choice.

math_code.why: Theorem-applying problems with a numeric/boolean/list answer checked automatically, like math; about half is applied physics/EE/finance instead of pure maths, and no code.

theoremqa.summary: TheoremQA (EMNLP 2023): 800 questions built around 350+ theorems in maths, physics, EE&CS and finance; answers are integer 216, float 378, bool 115, lists 73, option 18. 53 questions carry an image (drop them for Yugos). Short prompts (median about 160 characters). Useful as university-STEM exact-answer items for math and for hle/mmlu_pro-like chat; guess floor reflects the yes/no and option answers.

chat.why: University maths with a judged final answer touches only the maths share of hle.

math_code.why: One text problem to a boxed final answer, like math/arxivmath, on university topics (precalculus to multivariable calculus and series); graded by an LLM judge against a reference solution, not exact match; 200 of 1,100 need an image.

u_math.summary: U-MATH (Dec 2024): 1,100 previously unpublished university maths problems from real teaching materials, 6 topics, 900 text-only and 200 with images; free-form answers judged by an LLM (o3-mini in the paper). The 900 text problems are good fresh maths items. Per-question outcomes are limited: mu-MATH has 1,084 expert-labelled solutions from 4 models (Llama-3.1 70B, Qwen2.5 72B, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro) on 271 problems. o1 reached 93.1% on the text part.

chat.why: different skill: choosing function calls, not answering questions

math_code.why: different skill: function calling, no maths or code writing

agentic.why: JSON-schema tools in the prompt and the expected call compared by AST, with irrelevant/incomplete/error cases where no call is right, almost the bfcl shape; also 50 multi-turn/multi-step agent tasks with a simulated user graded on end state.

3.model: GPT-5 (High), ACEBench-en (metric not stated in that report)

acebench.summary: ACEBench (Jan 2025, answers fixed Oct 2025): tool-use test with 4,538 APIs; I counted 1,023 English items in 17 files (single/parallel calls, multi-turn, similar APIs, preferences, 6 parameter-type sets, 150 special cases with incomplete, wrong or irrelevant requests, 50 agent tasks), plus a parallel Chinese copy. It is the closest match to the public bfcl part. Median item about 3,400 characters with schemas. The GPT-5 score comes from another report (ERNIE 5.0) and is lower than the repo's GPT-4o score, so it is probably not the same metric.

chat.why: different skill: needs a live Linux shell to find the answer

math_code.why: Writing bash/python commands is code-like, but done step by step in a shell and graded on the answer or system state, not on one function with unit tests.

agentic.why: Multi-step tool use (one bash tool in a Docker box, up to 8+ rounds) graded on the final answer or a check script on the machine state, like the guessed private shape; topic is Linux admin, not API/customer-service tools.

level_guess.why: Paper scores (gpt-3.5-turbo 32.6%, gpt-4 42.4% on 144 tasks) were on tasks the Inspect port later found broken; on the fixed Inspect v4 test split (the one Yugos runs) glm-5.3-flash scored 95.8% and deepseek-v4-flash 97.5% (N=119), so most tasks are easy for any recent model. No group 1-2 score on the fixed tasks, so lower levels are estimated.

agent_bench_os.questions_where: https://github.com/THUDM/AgentBench/tree/main/data/os_interaction/data (fixed copy in the inspect_evals package, agent_bench/data)
agent_bench_os.summary: AgentBench OS (Aug 2023): 26 dev + 119 test tasks (Inspect v4; 144 in the paper) where the model uses a bash shell in a Docker machine to answer a question (count users, find an interval) or change the system, checked by answer match or a check script. It is in Yugos's runnable catalog (inspect_evals agent_bench_os, test split), so it may be one source of the hidden agentic questions (not confirmed); it needs Docker to run. Local copy: /root/cic/sn34-yugos/research/benchmarks/catalog/agent_bench_os.

chat.why: different skill: producing an API call, not an answer

math_code.why: different skill: API calling, no maths or code writing

agentic.why: API descriptions plus dialogue history in the prompt and one call to produce, checked by running it, close to bfcl single-turn; but text API descriptions and a [Name(key=value)] format instead of JSON schemas, and few no-call cases.

api_bank.summary: API-Bank (EMNLP 2023): evaluation set of 73 runnable APIs, 314 dialogues and 753 API calls in three levels (call, retrieve+call, plan+retrieve+call), plus a 1,888-dialogue training set. Each item gives API descriptions and the dialogue so far and asks for the next API request (level-1 file: 399 items, median about 2,000 characters). Good BFCL-like extra data; scores top out near 76% even for GPT-4o, likely label noise, so it separates models weakly.

chat.why: different skill: multi-turn customer-service tool dialogues

math_code.why: different skill: tool use, no maths or code writing

agentic.why: tau-bench style retail/airline conversations with a policy, tools and many calls, just like the guessed private shape; but they are training trajectories with no grader shipped (calls can be matched turn by turn, end-state needs the tau-bench environment) and long policy prompts.

apigen_mt.licence: cc-by-nc-4.0 (card also says: research use only; part generated with GPT-4, not to be used to build models that compete with OpenAI; card asks users to accept terms)
apigen_mt.summary: APIGen-MT-5k (Apr 2025): 5,000 verified multi-turn agent dialogues (human, function_call, observation, gpt turns, plus tools and the domain policy) generated with GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 in the tau-bench retail and airline environments; a training set for xLAM-2, not a test. Closest in shape to the guessed hidden agentic tasks (tau2-like), but there are no model scores per task, no difficulty data, and the non-commercial / no-competing-model terms must be checked before using it for router training.

chat.why: different skill: long interactive app tasks

math_code.why: The agent writes Python that calls app APIs and is checked by unit tests, but step by step in an environment over many turns, not one function from one prompt.

agentic.why: Multi-step everyday-app tasks (9 apps, 457 APIs) graded on the final database state, including damage checks, like the guessed private shape; but the agent calls tools by writing code over about 30-60 turns with long API docs.

appworld.questions_where: https://github.com/StonyBrookNLP/appworld (appworld download data; test splits ship in encrypted bundles)
appworld.results_where: https://github.com/StonyBrookNLP/appworld (appworld download experiment-outputs: per-task evaluation reports for the baseline runs)
appworld.licence: Apache-2.0, plus: protected data may be redistributed only in encrypted form
appworld.summary: AppWorld (ACL 2024): 750 tasks over 9 simulated apps (music, payments, mail, notes...) for about 100 fake users; the agent writes Python calling 457 APIs and is graded by state-based unit tests. In Yugos's catalog but only 'planned' (needs the AppWorld server). Leaderboard: GPT-4o ReAct 48.8% (normal) / 30.2% (challenge); 2026 harnesses reach 85-94% (Claude Opus 4.6 91.1%, GLM-5.3 94.0%). Test data is encrypted and must not be posted in plain text; baseline per-task outputs are downloadable.

chat.why: Short real-life information questions with a short answer and partial-credit scoring (like hotpotqa F1), but they are meant to be solved by browsing current websites, so closed-book answers are mostly wrong or stale.

agentic.why: Multi-step tool use, but live web browsing over many pages and graded on the final answer, not tools given in the prompt or an end state.

assistantbench.questions_where: https://huggingface.co/datasets/AssistantBench/AssistantBench (answers only for the 33 dev tasks; 181 test answers hidden)
assistantbench.summary: AssistantBench (Jul 2024): 214 realistic, time-consuming web tasks (e.g. which of a person's social accounts has most followers) with short answers scored with partial credit; only 33 dev answers are public. Hard and noisy for Yugos: it needs a live browser, answers drift with the web, and even GPT-5 with a browser agent gets 35%. HAL has encrypted traces for 15 model runs; whether they hold per-task scores was not checked.
